utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Call the case please, Mr. Court Deputy.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Good morning, Your Honours. This is Case Number IT-02-60-T, the Prosecutor versus Vidoje Blagojevic and Dragan Jokic.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Thank you. Good morning, ladies and gentlemen. Good morning, Witness. Did you have a good rest?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Are you ready to start?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Thank you. We won't keep you long today. Well, Mr. Shin, any cross-examination?

utterances.speaker: MR. SHIN
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. President. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. SHIN
utterances.text: Cross-examined by Mr. Shin:

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Good morning, Mr. Janjic.

utterances.speaker: MILE JANJIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Good morning.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: I'd like to begin by asking you some questions about the 12th of July when you were gathered with some other military policemen in front of the military police building, which is in front of the Bratunac Brigade headquarters. Now, we've heard from one of the military policemen who went into Potocari on that day that he had been ordered to go into Potocari and secure buses. Was that one of the orders that you had received?

utterances.speaker: MILE JANJIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Do you know if any of the other military policemen, any of your colleagues, had received that order?

utterances.speaker: MILE JANJIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: I'm sorry. You don't know whether they have or you -- you're saying that they didn't receive that order, that you know they didn't?

utterances.speaker: MILE JANJIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I wish to say that I don't know.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you. We've also heard that this military policeman had been told -- I'm sorry. There's apparently something wrong with this mike. Is that okay? We've also been told that that military policeman was told when issued that order there would be other people from the Bratunac Brigade, apart from the military police, in Potocari. Were you told anything like that?

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Could we have a name of the police officer because I take it the police officer has testified, at least from the flavour of the questions. So if we could have a name so we can double-check the bona fides of this particular assertion.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Well, generally speaking, it's not necessary. But if you request, Mr. Shin, could you provide the name to this witness.

utterances.speaker: MR. SHIN
utterances.text: Certainly. The witness is Mr. Radenko Zaric and the precise page number for the point I just raised. I'm not sure what the first few ERN numbers are but the last four are 9881, which should be adequate to identify the specific page.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. SHIN
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Mr. Janjic, should I repeat that question or are you able to answer?

utterances.speaker: MILE JANJIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Would you please repeat your question.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: When you were given your orders at the MP building, were you told that there would be other people from the Bratunac Brigade there, apart from the military police, in Potocari?

utterances.speaker: MILE JANJIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Orders were not received at that moment in terms of what should be done. We were called in to report in order to receive orders as to what we would do afterwards. As I said yesterday, it was a telephone call; it was not an order.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: But in any case, you don't -- or you're saying you weren't told that there would be other people, not as an order but just as information, that there would be other people from the Bratunac Brigade in Potocari on that day?

utterances.speaker: MILE JANJIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: When you got to Potocari on that day or through the course of let's say the 12th of July, did you see other people from the Bratunac Brigade present there?

utterances.speaker: MILE JANJIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Do you know what units of the Bratunac Brigade they were from?

utterances.speaker: MILE JANJIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know about that. It was very brief. I explained that yesterday. Zuti Most, Potocari. At one point in time, I did notice some members of the Bratunac Brigade. I don't know exactly which unit, but I do know that they are from the Bratunac Brigade; that I know for sure. But then after that, I didn't see them again. So I don't know anything about that.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did you see anyone from the Bratunac Brigade providing security in the area?

utterances.speaker: MILE JANJIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And you yourself, you were occupied in this counting process on the 12th of July. Is that correct? Let me be clear: Were there any other tasks you did on the 12th of July, apart from counting?

utterances.speaker: MILE JANJIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Only the counting.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And that would be true for the 13th of July as well, just the counting?

utterances.speaker: MILE JANJIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Now, you told us that you had seen the separation of the men from the women and children.

utterances.speaker: MILE JANJIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And you explained that you didn't see any abuse in that process.

utterances.speaker: MILE JANJIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Just so we're clear, we've heard evidence here that -- from a member of the DutchBat, that in the process of the separation on one occasion, there was a boy who was grabbed by the throat by -- I'm sorry, we're having some trouble with this mike. It's apparently the water. Is that okay? I'm sorry. I'll start my question again. We've heard evidence here from a member of the Dutch Battalion there that there were abuses in the separation process, and one example was of a boy who was grabbed by the throat as a means of pulling him away from the rest of the refugees. Did you see anything like that?

utterances.speaker: MILE JANJIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I did not see any such thing, but that is not to say that I am asserting that no such thing ever happened.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And in the course of the separations, did you hear -- did you hear any emotional outbursts? Did you hear any women crying?

utterances.speaker: MILE JANJIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And do you remember why they were crying?

utterances.speaker: MILE JANJIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, basically it was because they were leaving their homes, going to something quite uncertain. Most of them were not from Srebrenica originally, from the pre-war municipality of Srebrenica. Most of them had come from Bratunac and other places. So this hurt them. They were leaving their homes yet again and they didn't know where they were going.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Okay. But I was asking about the separation process.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: That's not true, Your Honour. That's not what he asked. Had he asked specifically. Earlier he talked about the separation. So to be fair to the gentleman, he needs to include that in.

utterances.speaker: MR. SHIN
utterances.text: I'm sorry, Your Honour. The question I asked exactly says: "In the course of the separations.". I'm not quite sure what was unclear to Mr. Karnavas.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Yes, I think he is still within the context. You may proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. SHIN
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Mr. Janjic, I was asking about in the course of the separations, did you hear any women crying because their husbands were being pulled away or because their sons were being pulled away?

utterances.speaker: MILE JANJIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I understand the question now. The answer I gave before was the way I had understood it then, so my answer now is no. I did not hear that they were pointing out that it was on account of that.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Okay. You didn't hear that, but did you see women crying as men -- as their husbands, their brothers, or their children were being pulled away from them? Did you see that? You saw the separation process, or at least part of it.

utterances.speaker: MILE JANJIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: As I mentioned yesterday, the separation took place about a hundred or 150 metres away from me, so I saw the process evolve. The men were going in the opposite direction, and the women went in my direction. So it's not that I could see the tears, see the emotions.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And you saw because they were, I think, coming towards you, you saw the men who had been separated. Right?

utterances.speaker: MILE JANJIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't understand the question.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Let me put it this way: You saw that separate group of men on the other side of the road, the men who had been separated. Right?

utterances.speaker: MILE JANJIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did you see among them old men, men as old as 60 or 65? We've heard evidence that there were men that old in that group.

utterances.speaker: MILE JANJIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And did you see men or perhaps children as young as 14 or 15 in that group?

utterances.speaker: MILE JANJIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Not that, no.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: We've heard evidence of that as well. Did you see any men in that group who were physically disabled?

utterances.speaker: MILE JANJIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know what you mean when you say "disabled." Disabled people, as far as I know, are people in wheelchairs and people who cannot walk, who have another obvious disability. I could not see whether somebody had some kind of disability. The answer is that I did not see anyone with -- in a wheelchair, with a prosthesis or something like that.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Okay. That was my question. So, you didn't see any of that. Could you see anyone that, as far as you could tell, was mentally handicapped among that group of men?

utterances.speaker: MILE JANJIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. I didn't notice any such thing.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Now, from what you could see of the separation process, did you see any DutchBat soldiers in that area or during that separation process? Could you see them from where you were?

utterances.speaker: MILE JANJIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did you see them trying to interfere with the separation, in particular in the cases where the very old or the very young were being taken away?

utterances.speaker: MILE JANJIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: As far as these UNPROFOR soldiers are concerned and the fact that they were going in the direction where these people were going, so it was away from me, as far as they're concerned, I could see that they were carrying stretchers, that they were transporting some people on these stretchers, that they were carrying water, water most often. I could not notice any other details. I didn't really notice anything.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Okay. Just so we're clear, did you see any DutchBat soldiers trying to prevent a man or a boy being taken away from their family?

utterances.speaker: MILE JANJIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I did not notice.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: At any point did you see anyone from the Dutch Battalion trying to get onto the buses that the men were being put on?

utterances.speaker: MILE JANJIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: So then you wouldn't be aware if any of them had been dissuaded from that at gunpoint?

utterances.speaker: MILE JANJIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, I didn't see any such thing. I didn't notice any such thing. Now, whether such things happened or not is not something I can claim at this stage because I could not keep the entire situation under control.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: So the separation process you saw from where you were, there were no beatings of men in the process?

utterances.speaker: MILE JANJIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: No one was kicked in that process?

utterances.speaker: MILE JANJIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Now, I'd like to move to a slightly later point in time, and perhaps we could start by taking a look at a short video clip.

utterances.speaker: MR. SHIN
utterances.text: I'm sorry, Your Honour, just one moment while I get the exhibit number. This is from Prosecution Exhibit P21. And we'll be playing it from Sanction.

utterances.speaker: MR. SHIN
utterances.text: I'll just wait a minute for the lights. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Does that -- that scene that you saw on the video clip, does that look familiar to you? Do you remember that?

utterances.speaker: MILE JANJIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: To tell you the truth, I don't even know what I saw. I saw the luggage I mentioned yesterday in front of the gate, the thing I mentioned yesterday. If I saw that right, it was just very brief. And the piles of rucksacks and things like that that I referred to yesterday around the gate. I think that that's it.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Okay. I'm sorry, just before we continue on this, so we're clear, the separations that you saw on the 12th and the 13th of July you didn't see a single incident of abuse? Not a single person being hit? Not a single person being kicked? Is that what you're saying?

utterances.speaker: MILE JANJIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I never claimed that no one had ever been kicked or hit with a hand. You asked me whether I saw something like that; I did not.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you. That's exactly what my question was, in fact. Did you ever hear of anyone being beaten or kicked then?

utterances.speaker: MILE JANJIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You never heard about it then; you never heard about it later?

utterances.speaker: MILE JANJIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Now, I showed you the video clip because you explained to us yesterday about this place where the men were being held, and as you just explained now the situation with the luggage. You mentioned as well -- you told us yesterday that your understanding was that the luggage was being left there for security reasons. Is that right?

utterances.speaker: MILE JANJIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Now, can you remind us: How far were you from where those men were in that building, in the yard of that building?

utterances.speaker: MILE JANJIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I've already said yesterday that it was about 100 metres away from me, this gate that we saw just now, perhaps even a bit more than that. And the yard extends to the place where I stood. So it's on the other side of the yard, the gate that they went through and where they left those things.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: So the yard extended up to where you were. So were you able to see the faces of some of the men being held there?

utterances.speaker: MILE JANJIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: At the moment when the yard was filled -- I mean, as it was getting filled, the people were getting closer and closer to me, very close to me. So there was only the fence that separated us. I cannot tell you exactly what the distance involved was, a couple of metres, up to 10 metres.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: So the men who were closest to you when you were -- when you saw them, how did they look to you? Would you say that they were scared?

utterances.speaker: MILE JANJIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I could not tell. I can't really give an answer to that.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Well, you did tell us yesterday that there was a point when you heard people in the yard saying things like: Why are you separating us? Maybe you are about to kill us. Was that an indication to you, perhaps, that these men were scared?

utterances.speaker: MILE JANJIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: If I understood you correctly, you are asking me what I could see in those people's faces. As for the shouting, that happened afterwards and I think that I explained that in greater detail yesterday. My understanding was that at that moment what my conclusion was, judging by people's faces and the expressions on their faces.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Generally speaking, Mr. Janjic, I'm asking about what you saw and what your understanding of the situation was, because we've had plenty of other evidence about these events. So I'm asking you, even though it happened later, did you hear comments such as: Are you about to kill us? Did that help you understand what the state of mind was, as far as you could see, of these men?

utterances.speaker: MILE JANJIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I have conveyed their words. I can repeat those words, but then it is for you to interpret it. Try to put yourself in their position and understand how they felt. What I can do is repeat what I have already said.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And, Mr. Janjic, I'm asking you now to interpret those words as you understood them, as you understood them.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Your Honour. Yesterday when I asked the gentleman to interpret the words of Colonel Jankovic where he stated that his belief was that they should be shown to the -- the media should be shown how well they were treated, to get the gentleman to tell us that at least Colonel Jankovic's state of mind was that nothing was going to happen to anybody, I got an objection from the gentleman. Now today he wants to have this gentleman interpret somebody else's state of mind. So if it wasn't -- if the objection was sustained yesterday, it should be sustained today. If the gentleman thought he was incapable of reading Colonel Jankovic's state of mind --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Well, Mr. Karnavas, I think you passed the limits at this moment.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Well, I think I'm right on the line, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: I think the Prosecution is just asking about the understanding of this witness, his personal understanding.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: All right. Very well, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: You may proceed, Mr. Shin.

utterances.speaker: MR. SHIN
utterances.text: Very well.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: When you heard these words: "Why are you separating us? Maybe you're about to kill us?", you described that as some sort of mutiny. Is that right? I think those were your exact words: Some sort of a mutiny.

utterances.speaker: MILE JANJIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, some reactions, some revolt, rebellion.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And that's when Colonel Jankovic spoke to them and told them that they would be transported?

utterances.speaker: MILE JANJIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: He said: It has already been said. Maybe you've already heard about this. So he meant that somebody had already said something and believed that they had heard it, too, that there would be no problem, that they would meet up with their families. Those were his words. That's what I said yesterday.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Just moving forward now to the next day, the same place, that building in the yard where the men are being held. When you arrived on the 13th of July, the yard was now empty you said. Did you see whether the luggage was still in the yard?

utterances.speaker: MILE JANJIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: In front of the yard there was some luggage scattered about, not too much of it. At the moment when it was being put there, I should say -- well, yes, there was. Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: So there was still luggage. Would it be fair to say that there was still luggage piled up by the gate? I'm sorry, you're nodding. If you could please just say yes or no for the record.

utterances.speaker: MILE JANJIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I didn't notice anything.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: I'm not sure if we misunderstood each other because you just said something about luggage. And my question to you is: Is it fair to say that there was still luggage piled up by the gate of this yard on the morning of the 13th of July, when you got there?

utterances.speaker: MILE JANJIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I didn't understand what you meant when you said "piled." I thought you meant something organised but, you know, there was scattered luggage where women had passed by, they had thrown their bags away, also by the canals. I'm not going into that whether people had one, two, or three bags, but they were scattered about.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Let's try to make this simple then. You told us that there was luggage left by the men - you thought it was for security reasons - by the gate of that yard on the 12th of July. Was that luggage still there when you returned on the 13th of July?

utterances.speaker: MILE JANJIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I did not observe.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You mentioned that, maybe not in the context of that yard exactly, but perhaps in the yard, other places, that the women -- that there were bags that you thought the women had left. Did you think that the women had thrown these bags away. Is that what you were saying? And please correct me if I'm wrong.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Objection. It calls for speculation, Your Honour. He's asking the gentleman to comment on what he thinks the women were doing. It's speculative.

utterances.speaker: MR. SHIN
utterances.text: Mr. President, the gentleman has told us that "there was scattered luggage where women had passed by. They had thrown their bags away." So I'm just asking a follow-up question on that, what the witness himself has said.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Yes, there may be some relations between the two. You may proceed, Mr. Shin.

utterances.speaker: MR. SHIN
utterances.text: Very well.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: So your understanding is that these bags that were scattered about, they were thrown away by the women?

utterances.speaker: MILE JANJIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, you're asking me to speculate. I told you: There were some, not many. There were some along the road. There were some in the ditch. All sorts of water-bottles, all sort of weights. It was like a dump. And if you want a precise answer, if I understood you correctly at all, whether somebody grabbed bags from their shoulders, telling them this they couldn't carry anything, the answer is no.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You didn't see anything like that on the 12th? You didn't see anything like that on the 13th?

utterances.speaker: MILE JANJIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: We've heard evidence that in addition to the luggage being left where the men were, that -- where the men were being held, there were also documentation that was left in the yard, ID cards, passports. Did you see any of that?

utterances.speaker: MILE JANJIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did you see anyone writing down the names of the male detainees?

utterances.speaker: MILE JANJIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did you ever see a list of them, the male detainees, at any point?

utterances.speaker: MILE JANJIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, no.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. Janjic. I'd like to move to a slightly different area. Now, you explained yesterday when you went down to Potocari on the 12th of July, that you went down in what you called the first group and that there were 10 or 15 military policemen. Just so we understand, how many military policemen were given this assignment on the 12th of July to go into Potocari?

utterances.speaker: MILE JANJIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: In that phone call, the police platoon was asked to come to the Zuti Most and take over. I came, passing by the petrol station, to the Zuti Most, which is yellow bridge. I described my meeting with Nikolic at the checkpoint. The trip by that vehicle to Potocari, after which the vehicle went back to pick up other people. And Nikolic, after giving an assignment to the first group, disappeared. The vehicle was already gone, and whether Nikolic met up with other groups and gave them some other assignments, I don't know. I can only tell you about the assignments given to the first group; for that, I was an eyewitness. I cannot speculate about other assignments.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Mr. Janjic, I'm not asking you to speculate. I'm asking you whether apart from those 10 to 15 military police officers there were other military police officers who went into Potocari on that day. Do you know that?

utterances.speaker: MILE JANJIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, no.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Now, you spent all of the 12th and all of the 13th in this counting process, and you mentioned that some other military policemen were involved in as well. How many military policemen were involved in this counting process, all 10 or 15?

utterances.speaker: MILE JANJIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I think I already explained that. Do you want me to repeat? Do we have time for that?

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Maybe if you could just answer the question, we could move on quickly past this. Were all of you involved in the counting or just some of you?

utterances.speaker: MILE JANJIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I was there. There were other members of the military police. For a while they stayed, and then they left to take up another assignment. In the end, I was left there alone.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: So if I understand you correctly, at some point all of you were involved in the counting process, and then at some point you were the only one involved in the counting process?

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Objection.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: The gentleman neither stated yesterday nor today. Yesterday he was very clear. So either allow the gentleman to restate what he said yesterday, since clearly, you know, they don't like the answer. Or be fair to the gentleman. But he never stated that all of them were involved in the counting, and I believe Mr. Shin had overnight to look at the transcript and has the transcript, so he knows exactly what the gentleman said yesterday.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Well, I believe that Mr. Shin is just asking a question to clarify something from the answer of this witness. Let us proceed. I think the witness could answer by yes or no.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: I'm sure the witness can answer by yes or no, Your Honour. I have no problem, and I don't want to debate the point. But Mr. Shin has the transcript and he knows what the gentleman stated. And the gentleman never stated that all of them. And it appears now that he doesn't like the answer and is trying to trick the witness.

utterances.speaker: MR. SHIN
utterances.text: Mr. President, that is entirely uncalled for. I was simply asking this witness a question. There is absolutely no reason to argue whether I was happy or unhappy with this question; I'm simply clarifying something from yesterday.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Yes, you may proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. SHIN
utterances.text: Thank you. And just for the record, I would note that the witness did in fact respond to the question with a "yes," although it doesn't appear on the transcript. So I'll ask the question again.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Mr. Janjic, and you can explain further if necessary, at some point were all 10 or 15 of this group involved in the counting and then at some point there was just you involved in the counting. Is that what you're saying?

utterances.speaker: MILE JANJIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: At the moment when I received my assignment from Colonel Jankovic, I was involved and others, those who happened to be there at the moment, we counted the people who were getting into the buses. That lasted for an hour or two. After that, most of the other members received another assignment left by that vehicle in another direction, and I was left alone to continue the counting. They were there only for a while to help me in the counting. That's what I explained before.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Okay. And just to clarify, very specifically, you say: You and others were involved in the counting. When you say "others," do you mean all the others?

utterances.speaker: MILE JANJIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I was talking about the first group of policemen, including me. Call it my group. We were there. The first group did the counting. After a while, most of my colleagues were sent elsewhere and I and a couple of other men were left to continue the counting.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: So in fact it wasn't just you left with the counting; it was you and a couple of other policemen from your group? I'm not -- this isn't meant to be complicated. I'm just trying to clarify something you told us yesterday.

utterances.speaker: MILE JANJIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. In the end I was left alone with only a couple of other policemen from my group.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Now, this counting process, you explained to us yesterday you started it one way, and then you devised and proposed to Colonel Jankovic a different way of doing the counting. Just a question on that first method that you were using. Just so we're clear, in that first method, were you counting individual person by individual person? Is that what you were doing?

utterances.speaker: MILE JANJIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And you found that difficult, so the second method you were doing you were counting vehicle by vehicle and then multiplying by the average number of people who could be in any given vehicle. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: MILE JANJIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: So the first counting system was an exact count, and the second count is actually an approximate count. Is that right?

utterances.speaker: MILE JANJIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I cannot be 100 per cent sure, even about the first system, that it was right and accurate if we go into detail.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Sorry. I'm speaking before the interpretation is complete. But the second counting in any case was an approximate counting system. That's fair, isn't it?

utterances.speaker: MILE JANJIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Very approximate, but fairly accurate.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Now, how did you know what the average number of people who could fit on any given vehicle was? How did you know that?

utterances.speaker: MILE JANJIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, we knew because in the previous count we counted every vehicle, including ten buses, five or six trucks, and always the number was the same with a margin of difference of five to six people, never more than ten.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Now, from time to time you would go, as you explained to Colonel Jankovic, and give him a figure for the number of people you had counted. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: MILE JANJIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. At the moment while we were waiting for the vehicles when the space in front of us was clear, when we had no other jobs to do, when the trucks were just arriving and getting parked.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: On these occasions -- well, approximately how many times do you think you went to Colonel Jankovic to tell him whatever figure you had?

utterances.speaker: MILE JANJIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I cannot be certain. Not during every break, but after every 10 or 15 -- couple of times during the day.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Sorry. I'll wait until the interpretation ends before continuing. On any of these occasions, did Colonel Jankovic tell you to do something, something different in response to what you told him the number was?

utterances.speaker: MILE JANJIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Do you mean a specific date?

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Either the 12th or the 13th you would give him the number. On hearing the number, would he tell you to do something different or change your instructions in any way?

utterances.speaker: MILE JANJIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. I just mentioned one comment concerning the figures. That was on the morning of the 13th. I mentioned that member of the MUP who was also giving him numbers. And at that point, he suggested that we should be more careful about the figures, that they should match, that we should be more serious in doing our job.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: So would it be fair to say that Colonel Jankovic actually -- he didn't really respond to the numbers you were giving him, he just -- you reported to him and that was it?

utterances.speaker: MILE JANJIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: What do you mean he didn't really respond?

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: He didn't tell you -- he didn't give you any orders as a result of the numbers provided to him?

utterances.speaker: MILE JANJIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Now, you spent all day on the 12th of July, all day on the 13th of July in this counting process. You must have asked him at some point what the purpose of these numbers were?

utterances.speaker: MILE JANJIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Now, you mentioned that for the first day the final figure was 9.000 and then some hundreds. You also mentioned that -- I believe you mentioned that you counted the men on both days as well. How many men did you count on that first day, if you can recall?

utterances.speaker: MILE JANJIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't think you actually followed what I was saying yesterday. I never counted the men.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: I'm sorry --

utterances.speaker: MILE JANJIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I -- or do you mean the women? Who do you mean? I was counting buses. I think I was clear enough.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Yes. Let me rephrase. You counted the number of buses with -- after you changed your counting system, you counted the number of buses with men on them?

utterances.speaker: MILE JANJIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Buses, yes. I said there were 10 or 15 buses, between 10 and 15 on the first day, if you're asking me about the first day.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: So to come up with a total number of men from that first day, using your system you just multiplied the number of buses by the average number of men that a bus could take. Correct?

utterances.speaker: MILE JANJIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: We knew the average number that could fit into a bus or a truck as of that morning. I didn't need to calculate the average throughout the day. We would just mark the number of buses and multiply it with the average of passengers that fitted into a bus. So 10 or 15 multiplied by the average.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Well, Mr. Shin, I think there is still something that is unclear, at least to my mind. Who are on those buses, women or men?

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Mr. Janjic, I'm asking now just about the buses with men on them. And with this process, this system that you explained, on the first day how many men would you calculate left on buses?

utterances.speaker: MILE JANJIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: There were 10 to 15 buses.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Okay. And what was the average number of people per bus? And I'm just talking about the men now.

utterances.speaker: MILE JANJIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: The average number of people that could fit into buses, trucks, and the rest I cannot remember. I knew it then, but I can no longer recall it. Because there were two types of trucks, two types of buses -- in fact, there was one type of truck -- one type of bus and two types of trucks.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Well, on that first day you said there were 10 to 15 buses. Now, isn't it right that a bus can take approximately 50 people?

utterances.speaker: MILE JANJIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, I cannot be certain about the figure, but I'm certain that there were more than 50 people per bus.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you. On the second day, just the men now, how many buses were there?

utterances.speaker: MILE JANJIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I cannot tell you anything about the second day, because if you followed my testimony, starting from noon, one series of buses started to leave, then a second series of buses. It was not like the first day. From noon onwards, buses started going back and forth. It was not like on the first day. They were making round trips on the second day.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Okay. Let's turn to this man from the MUP you just -- you mentioned a short while ago who was also counting. Now, was he part of your team as well? Was he telling you the figures he was coming with up?

utterances.speaker: MILE JANJIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. He did not tell me anything and he was not a part of our team; that much is certain.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: But you did compare occasionally the numbers he was coming up with and the numbers that you were coming up with?

utterances.speaker: MILE JANJIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I did never mention that I compared my numbers with his.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: I'm sorry. I thought you said that he came to you and said your numbers needed to be more precise, which sounds to me like there was a comparison of numbers.

utterances.speaker: MILE JANJIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: That was a comment made my Colonel Jankovic; that's what I explained a moment ago. On the morning of the 13th, that policeman was close to Colonel Jankovic. I could not overhear their conversation. But when I reported to Colonel Jankovic with my first numbers, he said that we need to be more accurate. And I am still not sure whether he meant me or him.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Now, you say that you don't remember the exact number of buses that left on the 13th of July. Do you remember approximately how many bus loads left on that day, just approximately?

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Thank you. The question was asked and answered several times. He gave a detailed answer saying that the buses were turning around. Now he's asking the gentleman to guess. He already answered no, but I would appreciate if the Prosecutor would stop asking the witness to just guess at figures. Now, if he wants to ask him what the overall figure at the end of the day, and then he can come up with some kind of a figure, that's fine.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Well, Mr. Shin, I think this question is asked.

utterances.speaker: MR. SHIN
utterances.text: Okay. I'll move on, Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Now, Mr. Janjic, you testified on the 12th of July in Potocari, a Pinzgauer arrived and part of the military policemen got into that. Approximately how many men was that?

utterances.speaker: MILE JANJIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I cannot be precise. The Pinzgauer was full, so it was not one or two men, it was more.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And how many men can a Pinzgauer carry?

utterances.speaker: MILE JANJIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I cannot specify. I believe five, six, seven men can fit, certainly, but I'm not sure. Because it is a combat vehicle. It carries this weapon, so you need the gunner, the crew. I really don't want to go into any estimates. There is the driver, the driver's assistant.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: I think your answer will suffice. Now, you said that you did not know where they went. Did you find out later where that vehicle had gone?

utterances.speaker: MILE JANJIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Only from what they told me.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And what did they tell you?

utterances.speaker: MILE JANJIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: They said they had been on a mission, they were accompanying General Mladic to some positions around Jogor [phoen], that is a position that I never visited -- Viogor, in fact, Viogor. It is the municipality of Srebrenica.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: I'd like to turn now to your task on the evening of the 13th of July, which was guarding these buses in Bratunac. Now, you explained to us that you were guarding three buses and a truck during that evening, during that night. Did you at any point exchange any words with the people on the bus? I mean, you're from Bratunac and they might have been from the region.

utterances.speaker: MILE JANJIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I did exchange some words, but not in terms of introducing myself to him or finding out about him. It was a very small cramped space, the door was closed, nobody was allowed to come in or out. They were asking for things kindly. They were not hysterical. They were asking for water. We give -- gave them water. We found two buckets, two containers of 10 to 15 litres each. And my colleague and I gave this to them. After midnight, because we were sitting opposite the bakery, which was working all night, we got hold of a couple of loaves of bread and we gave that to them through the window. That was all the contact we had with them. We did not tell each other our names. They didn't look for that either.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Now, you didn't at any point check for the IDs of this people, did you?

utterances.speaker: MILE JANJIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You didn't at any point have a list of the detainees on that, did you, detainees on those buses?

utterances.speaker: MILE JANJIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Now, I'd like to show you a map of Bratunac, and this is Prosecution Exhibit 12.1.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Yes, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: The map itself has --

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Microphone for Mr. Karnavas, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: The map already notes places, so it's not just a blank map. So they're already somehow -- and other words, through other witnesses have placed who is -- you know, what is where. So I would like to know what the purpose is of showing him the map, because if they're trying to get him to identify a place which is already designated on the map, then clearly it's suggestive.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Well, I believe that this witness is from that area, so that will make no difference if some buildings were marked or not. We are testing the credibility of this witness concerning the location. But it will depend on -- I haven't seen this map yet, but it depends on what kind of marks are there. Could we have it.

utterances.speaker: MR. SHIN
utterances.text: Mr. President, it's an aerial of the town of Bratunac now. There are basic dates and basic places which we freely have been making reference to, both the Prosecution and the Defence. If the witness disagrees with the identification of any particular building, he's of course free to say so.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Yes. Could we have that map put on the ELMO, please.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Now, Mr. Janjic, this is an aerial of the town of Bratunac. Are you able to locate some of the places that you've mentioned on there? I'm going to ask you now: With this map, are you able to identify where those three buses and truck were that you were guarding on the night of the 13th of July?

utterances.speaker: MILE JANJIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Even if I can help you, I would need some time to find my way here and to see what this is all about.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Please go ahead and take a minute to orient yourself. If you're not able to orient yourself, please indicate that as well and I'll just go ahead with the question.

utterances.speaker: MILE JANJIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. It's a bit easier now. I can find my way now.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Is that -- you're pointing now to where the buses and trucks were?

utterances.speaker: MILE JANJIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I wasn't showing anything. I was just keeping my hands there for no reason.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Are you able to find where the buses and trucks were or not?

utterances.speaker: MILE JANJIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I can find the place where I was, where I was at the time, by those buses.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Would you point that out, please.

utterances.speaker: MILE JANJIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: It's across the street from the police station, 10 or 15 metres away.

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: The interpreters kindly ask the witness to repeat his question. It's hard to understand what he's saying.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] It's around the middle of the road, and then the police station is there and the Vuk Karadzic school is there. And then from the police station, about 20 or 30 metres into the street.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Okay. Thank you. Now --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Well, Mr. Shin, I think after I've even this map, I think there's some credit in the objections from Defence counsel. You could show this witness a map with the name of the locations and the buildings, but on this map it specifically in English indicated some words like "buses" there, which is very leading. I hope you -- in the future you could provide us with more clean maps.

utterances.speaker: MR. SHIN
utterances.text: Certainly, Mr. President, and we'll do this without the map then. Thank you, Madam Usher.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Mr. Janjic, you mentioned that you heard -- you told us you heard one burst of automatic gunfire coming from the direction of the Vuk Karadzic school, and that's all. Is that correct? You didn't hear any other shots coming from that school?

utterances.speaker: MILE JANJIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I never said that I heard one either. Again, you didn't follow what I was saying.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: I believe your exact words were that there was "one volley of automatic rifle fire."

utterances.speaker: MILE JANJIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: There is a big difference between a burst of gunfire and one single round of gunfire. It can be one shot, and it can be a thousand bullets. So there's a big difference between the two.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Sir, are you saying you might have heard as much as a thousand bullets being fired that night?

utterances.speaker: MILE JANJIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. I never said that. I said automatic gunfire, but I wasn't counting the actual bullets. And the street and the echoes that were heard, there was no way I could count all of that.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did you go to the school yourself, Mr. Janjic?

utterances.speaker: MILE JANJIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: What school?

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: The Vuk Karadzic school.

utterances.speaker: MILE JANJIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I never went to that school, if you're talking about those days, or rather, that particular evening.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: It's that particular evening I'm asking about.

utterances.speaker: MILE JANJIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did you ever hear later that there were 50 or more bodies that were collected from that school after that evening?

utterances.speaker: MILE JANJIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: This is the first time I hear about that from you, so the answer is no.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did you hear at any point that there were people being detained in the stadium? And we've heard evidence of that from several people now.

utterances.speaker: MILE JANJIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I was precise about this. When the task was received on the 13th in the evening, I don't think that anybody would have missed that. The security of the school was mentioned and the security of the streets, and then there is buses and trucks. Not to spell that out very precisely, but at no point was any football stadium mentioned. I did not have any suspicions, there was no need for me to go to that football stadium, so I don't know anything.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: So you never even heard later that there were people being detained at that stadium?

utterances.speaker: MILE JANJIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did you know that on the meeting at the Fontana Hotel on the 12th of July, that Mladic had said that people, the Muslim refugees, should be put in the Bratunac stadium. Did you ever hear that?

utterances.speaker: MILE JANJIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did you ever hear that in 1992 there were Muslims who were killed in that stadium?

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Your Honour, objection as to relevance. What is the relevance at this point in time?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Well, I think in the direct examination you asked this question.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: The question was with respect to 1995, in light of the new "evidence" from this -- the previous witness that they had on their case in-chief, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Which may be related to 1995.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Very well.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: If the Prosecution asks 1992 --

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Very well, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: But anyway, it's hearsay evidence.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: I understand, I understand, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Yes, you may proceed.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did you ever hear that, Mr. Janjic, that in 1992 Muslims were killed in that stadium?

utterances.speaker: MILE JANJIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Now, you were asked yesterday about the reburial operation that occurred later in 1995, in the fall of 1995. And you said you yourself were not involved in that. Do you know whether there were other military policemen who were involved in securing the road between Bratunac and Srebrenica and further down towards Zeleni Jadar? Do you know anything about that?

utterances.speaker: MILE JANJIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. No.

utterances.speaker: MR. SHIN
utterances.text: No further questions, Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. Shin. Well, Mr. Karnavas, we have five minutes left for this sitting. Can you finish your re-direct in five minutes?

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Your Honour, this cross calls for no re-direct.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Oh, even less than that. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Well, at this stage are there any documents to tender? Mr. Karnavas?

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: No, Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Thank you. Mr. Shin?

utterances.speaker: MR. SHIN
utterances.text: No, Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Thank you. Well, Witness, thank you very much for coming to The Hague to give your evidence. The usher will show you out of the room. We wish you a pleasant journey back home. You may go now.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you, too.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Well, Mr. Karnavas, would you please brief us about the next witness -- I mean, are there any protective measures?

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: None, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: I see. And how long are you going to take for the direct examination?

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: I am hopeful, I am hopeful, that we will -- I think we can handle it in one session, and perhaps with one session for cross, although my goal is to finish this witness today so we can kind of catch up on some ground. But we are not behind schedule. We will make up --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: We are one person in the schedule, which was left from last week.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Well, by the end of the week, Your Honour, I can assure you we will be back on schedule.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: I see. I see. Which means?

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: We will -- I -- tomorrow, I believe, we will be able to handle two witnesses, Your Honour, that's my expectation. The witnesses are in town, so logistically speaking we are well ahead of the schedule.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Thank you. I think it's time for us to break now and we will resume at quarter to 11.00.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Good morning, Witness.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Morning.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Would you please stand up and make the solemn declaration.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I solemnly declare that I will speak the truth, the whole truth, and nothing but the truth.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Thank you. You may sit down, please. Mr. Karnavas.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. President, Your Honours. Examined by Mr. Karnavas:

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Good morning, sir. Could you please tell us your name.

utterances.speaker: ZORAN JOVANOVIC
utterances.text: Zoran Jovanovic.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And could you please tell us your last name letter by letter.

utterances.speaker: ZORAN JOVANOVIC
utterances.text: J-o-v-a-n-o-v-i-c, with a diacritic.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you. Mr. Jovanovic, July 1995, were you a member of the Bratunac Brigade?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN JOVANOVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Could you please tell us what position you held in the Bratunac Brigade on July 1995.

utterances.speaker: ZORAN JOVANOVIC
utterances.text: I was commander of the 2nd Infantry Battalion.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: For how long did you hold that position? Were you the commander of the 2nd Infantry Battalion?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN JOVANOVIC
utterances.text: I was acting commander, actually.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Okay. Thank you. Now, could you please tell us how long you held that position.

utterances.speaker: ZORAN JOVANOVIC
utterances.text: About two months.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And prior to that, what was your position in the Bratunac Brigade?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN JOVANOVIC
utterances.text: I was assistant commander for intelligence and security matters in the battalion as well.

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Interpreters note, could the witness please be asked to speak up a bit.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You're going to need to raise your voice a little bit, even though the microphones can pick up. So I'm going to ask you to speak up a little louder. Okay?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN JOVANOVIC
utterances.text: I understand.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Have some water, relax. Okay. Now, I want to focus your attention to the period commencing with July 6, 1995, which was when the activities surrounding Srebrenica began. Could you please tell us, if you recall, whether you received any special instructions prior to July 6, concerning the activities that were about to begin against Srebrenica.

utterances.speaker: ZORAN JOVANOVIC
utterances.text: We were given instructions to raise the combat readiness level of the units in case our positions were attacked.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: All right. Now, your positions, where had they been prior to July 6?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN JOVANOVIC
utterances.text: You mean you want me to tell you where all units were, at which positions?

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Just basically. If you could just tell us, describe to us, where your positions were. And then we'll get to the map at some point.

utterances.speaker: ZORAN JOVANOVIC
utterances.text: Our positions were to the left of Zuti Most at Caus and Obadi and on the right, the villages of Obadi and Omanac between the towns of Bratunac and Potocari.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: If you know, could you please tell us how long did you have those positions, physically that is. How long had you been there, prior to July 6th now I'm speaking.

utterances.speaker: ZORAN JOVANOVIC
utterances.text: Well, from 1992 all the way up to 1995.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Now, on July 11th Srebrenica fell. Could you please tell us how far did you and your troops of the 2nd Battalion advance towards Srebrenica during that period.

utterances.speaker: ZORAN JOVANOVIC
utterances.text: The forces of the 2nd Battalion did not advance toward Srebrenica. We had another task, and our units were to move in a different direction.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you. Now, I want to show you a document, what has come into evidence as P406. If you could please look at it. Do you recognise this document, sir?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN JOVANOVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And what do you recognise the document to be?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN JOVANOVIC
utterances.text: This is an order that we got from the brigade command. Every battalion had its own separate tasks.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: All right. Now, I take it in this document we'll find a reference to your particular battalion, that is the 2nd Battalion of the Bratunac Brigade. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN JOVANOVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Could you please tell us on which paragraph, which numbered paragraph, is the reference to your particular --

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: That would be on page 3, Madam Usher, in the English version.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: All right. And this is the -- in this paragraph, it would describe your activities concerning the events surrounding Srebrenica. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN JOVANOVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Do you know for a fact whether the activities that are listed in paragraph 5.2 were actually carried out?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN JOVANOVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Okay. Now, if you could just -- if I could show you another document -- actually, before we get to it, this document would be D179. It is for identification purposes. Prior to July 6th, did you have any meetings at the command with the commander of the Bratunac Brigade? Before we get to the document, do you recall whether you had any meetings with the commander?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN JOVANOVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: All right. Now, I would like to direct your attention on this particular document, D179 for identification, and if you could look at the -- well, first of all, let me ask you: What have I just handed you? What is this document?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN JOVANOVIC
utterances.text: You gave me my work notebook.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: That's your handwriting?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN JOVANOVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Do you know where -- did you turn over that notebook to the Office of the Prosecution when they questioned you two years after Mr. Blagojevic had been indicted?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN JOVANOVIC
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Do you know where those notes were?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN JOVANOVIC
utterances.text: At the command of the Bratunac Brigade.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Is there any reason why you didn't try to destroy your notes?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN JOVANOVIC
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: All right. Fair enough. Now, if I could direct your attention to 3 July 1995, if you could look at in this document. And for us that would be on page 3 of this particular document with an ERN number of 00716489. Could you please look at the date that you have as 3 July 1995 and, in particular, if I could draw your attention to the section where it says: "Orders issued by brigade commander." And on your version the ERN number would be 01134047. Do you see that, sir?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN JOVANOVIC
utterances.text: I see that.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: That's your handwriting?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN JOVANOVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And could you please explain to us what you have written down. You don't need to read it to us, but what is -- what are the items that you have written down under: "Orders issued by the brigade commander"?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN JOVANOVIC
utterances.text: Tasks from the brigade commander.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And if you were to look at what you've noted down in your handwriting from a meeting that you had attended on 3 July 1995, sir, if you could look at that and compare it to the previous document I showed you, which has been marked and entered into evidence as P406. If you could compare those two, and specifically paragraphs number 5.2. Are they similar in nature? That is the tasks that were ordered.

utterances.speaker: ZORAN JOVANOVIC
utterances.text: Yes, yes, completely the same.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Okay. Thank you. Now, we won't be needing these two documents at this point in time.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Well, Mr. Karnavas.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: For the sake of the record, can you tell me how did you get this document.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honour. We got these from the Office of the Prosecution. These are documents that they had. The one -- the document that is the notes, his notes, the gentleman's notes, were apparently found by the Office of the Prosecution when they did a search of the Bratunac Brigade headquarters, hence the reason why I asked him whether he had destroyed the documents.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Okay.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Now, sir, I want to show you -- let me ask you this: Concerning the events which you were tasked to do - and you may have answered this question - do you recall whether you carried out these tasks, the tasks that were issued to you by your commander concerning the attack on Srebrenica?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN JOVANOVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: All right. From July 6th to July 11th, did you at any point in time go into Srebrenica?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN JOVANOVIC
utterances.text: No, I did not.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did you at any point in time move from your positions?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN JOVANOVIC
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: All right. Could you please tell us from where you were located what means of communications you had.

utterances.speaker: ZORAN JOVANOVIC
utterances.text: From the place where I was in that period, I had cable communication, telephone communication, and Motorola communication.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And who could you communicate --

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Microphone, please.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And who could you communicate with, with the telephone?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN JOVANOVIC
utterances.text: I had a telephone link with all the companies in the 2nd Battalion, with the command of the 2nd Battalion, and with the brigade command.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: When you say "the brigade command," would that be the one that's in Bratunac?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN JOVANOVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Could you communicate directly from your position to -- with that telephone that is, to Pribicevac, where the forward command -- the command post of the 3rd Battalion was normally located?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN JOVANOVIC
utterances.text: I don't know exactly. I had no need to communicate with Pribicevac, but I did have links with the brigade command.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Now, when you say you had "links with the brigade command," what are you speaking about? Is that the commander itself or the building itself?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN JOVANOVIC
utterances.text: The building.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: All right. Do you know whether from July 6th to July 11th you contacted your commander, Colonel Blagojevic?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN JOVANOVIC
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Other than the tasks that were ordered of you that we have seen in the order that was dated 5 July 1995, which correspond to your handwritten notes of July 3, 1995, during that period, that is July 6 to July 11, did you receive any additional orders or different orders?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN JOVANOVIC
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Now, we understand, and I think it's an established fact, that on July 11th, 1995, Srebrenica fell. Sir, did you on that particular day go into Srebrenica, yes or no?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN JOVANOVIC
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did you go into Potocari that day, and I'm speaking about the 11th?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN JOVANOVIC
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Moving to the 12th. Did you go into Potocari on July 12th, 1995?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN JOVANOVIC
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did you go into Srebrenica?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN JOVANOVIC
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: What about the 13th, on the 13th of July did you go into --

utterances.speaker: ZORAN JOVANOVIC
utterances.text: No, no.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Okay. Now, moving back to July 12th, at that point in time do you recall whether you had received any additional orders, that is orders other than the ones that are reflected in your handwritten notes of July 3rd and the ones that the commander gave formally in his order that's dated 5 July 1995?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN JOVANOVIC
utterances.text: Yes, yes. We received different orders.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Now, could you please explain to us first of all what those orders were.

utterances.speaker: ZORAN JOVANOVIC
utterances.text: Well, the orders were that our units should go to search the terrain up to certain points, up to certain places.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: All right. Were you given on that particular day specific exact coordinates, map coordinates, as to how far each company within the battalion should move?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN JOVANOVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Now, before we get into the exact locations to -- that you were to search and move to, could you please tell us first of all about what time of day would it have been when you received those orders.

utterances.speaker: ZORAN JOVANOVIC
utterances.text: I don't know the exact time, but it was in the course of the day.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Do you know from whom you received those orders, specifically, if you recall?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN JOVANOVIC
utterances.text: From the brigade command, but I cannot remember exactly who, which one of the officers.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Now, this might be an important question not worthy for the Prosecution. Could you please tell us: How did you receive those ordinaries.

utterances.speaker: ZORAN JOVANOVIC
utterances.text: By telephone.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: All right. Now, before again we go into where you were to move and search the terrain, could you please tell us whether you, yourself, as the acting commander of the 2nd Battalion of the Bratunac Brigade ordered any of your men to go into Potocari on that day.

utterances.speaker: ZORAN JOVANOVIC
utterances.text: No. Moreover, they strictly ordered us not to go in. Those were the orders.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: All right. Now, could you please tell us now company by company, and first we're going to -- I'm going to have you explain to us and then I'm going to have you show us, okay, if you could please explain to us what areas you and the other companies were to search on that particular day.

utterances.speaker: ZORAN JOVANOVIC
utterances.text: How do you want me to show you?

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: All right. Well, first I want you to explain to me. You had -- how many companies were there in the battalion?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN JOVANOVIC
utterances.text: We had five companies.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Now, could you please just tell us, just describe to us, where they were supposed to move to.

utterances.speaker: ZORAN JOVANOVIC
utterances.text: The 3rd and the 4th Company were in the area of Obadi village and Caus. And they were supposed to go in the direction of Potocari and to stop at the edge of the woods behind the factories in Potocari and to search that part of the terrain.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: All right. Now, just so we have a clear understanding, the two companies, the 3rd and 4th, are separated from the other companies by the road. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN JOVANOVIC
utterances.text: Yes. They were left of the road from Bratunac to Srebrenica.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: All right. So if we're going from Bratunac to Srebrenica, you come across the Zuti Most. There on the left side, up on the hill.

utterances.speaker: ZORAN JOVANOVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And then if we go to the right, again going from Bratunac to Srebrenica, that's where you would have the 2nd Company and the 1st Company. Correct?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN JOVANOVIC
utterances.text: The 2nd and the 5th and a part of the 1st, because most of the troops from the 1st Company were out in the field near Pjenovac or Pjenovica.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Now, what about -- what about the other companies? Where were they to search? We talked about the 3rd and the 4th. Now, what about the 2nd, the 5th, and part of the 1st?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN JOVANOVIC
utterances.text: The 1st, the 2nd, and the 5th Companies were to search Budak, Pale, Jaglic, and Bljcevica, the terrain around these villages.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: All right. Could you please tell us where were you located, in which of these companies, if any of them, were you located on the 12th of July, 1995.

utterances.speaker: ZORAN JOVANOVIC
utterances.text: I was with the 2nd and the 1st Companies at Zagoni.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Now, you said that - and I'm going to stick with the latter companies, the 1st, the 2nd, and the 5th - you indicated that they were to go to Budak, Pale, and then onwards. Could you please tell us if all of the members of these companies went in the same direction or took the same route to get to Budak and Pale?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN JOVANOVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Now, did all -- now, from your location could you please describe to us what route you took, what road you took, to get to -- to Budak and Pale.

utterances.speaker: ZORAN JOVANOVIC
utterances.text: From the defence line, which we held until then, we climbed down to the road to Bljeceva, which was about 300 metres away. And we took that road to go to Bljeceva.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Now, is that the same road that takes you from the Zuti Most towards Potocari, where you then take a right to go to Budak?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN JOVANOVIC
utterances.text: Yes, it is.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: So on that day did you go to Zuti Most on the asphalt road and then take a right?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN JOVANOVIC
utterances.text: No. I was at Zagoni, which is to the right of Zuti Most. And then from Zagoni you take a country road to the Potocari/Bljeceva road, so I had no need to go down there in order to get to Potocari.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And how many men were with you when you took that road?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN JOVANOVIC
utterances.text: Around 100 troops, taking into account the 2nd Company, part of the 1st, and the 5th Company, maybe a few more, but around 100.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Would you know whether any of the other members of the 2nd -- the 1st and the 2nd and the 5th Company took a different route to get to Budak?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN JOVANOVIC
utterances.text: The left wing of the 2nd Company was at Zuti Most, since they had to go towards Bljeceva, too, one part of that company crossed through Potocari.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: So they would have gone a different route, taken a different route?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN JOVANOVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And you said -- would they have gone all the way through Potocari or is there -- at some point do they veer off, off the road, to head towards Budak?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN JOVANOVIC
utterances.text: They did not go to Potocari. They turned right before Potocari to catch up with us.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Is there a particular reason why all of you, that is the 1st, the 2nd, and the 5th Company did not take the same route?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN JOVANOVIC
utterances.text: In front of the Defence line, there were minefields. And it would take a lot of time to clear the minefields, to remove the mines, to enable them to go through. We had to remove the mines at least in one section of that field to let the troops past.
