utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: All right. Did you all meet up in Budak or Pale?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN JOVANOVIC
utterances.text: No, not in Budak, not all of us. The left wing of the 2nd Company passed through Budak, and we all met up in Bljeceva.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: What were the concrete instructions, orders?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN JOVANOVIC
utterances.text: The orders were to search the terrain in the places that I mentioned a moment ago.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Had you searched the terrain before, prior to this?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN JOVANOVIC
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Had you been given any specific instructions on how the terrain should be searched?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN JOVANOVIC
utterances.text: Nothing specific. The orders only said that we should search the terrain to see if some of the enemy were left there.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Now, did you give any specific instructions as to how your men were to search the terrain?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN JOVANOVIC
utterances.text: Well, the troops were given orders to search the terrain; however, since there were minefields everywhere, both in front of our defence lines and in front of the enemy's defence line, nobody dared to do a proper search of the terrain. They mainly walked along the road towards Bljeceva.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Would you please tell us how long or how many days you were out there searching the terrain.

utterances.speaker: ZORAN JOVANOVIC
utterances.text: We covered that part of the terrain very quickly, and before dark we emerged at Pale village. We did not meet anyone. There was no resistance, and our job was done very quickly. And, as I said, we emerged at Pale before dark.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did you come across any abandoned weapons?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN JOVANOVIC
utterances.text: Well, we mostly found ammunition.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did you come across any dead bodies?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN JOVANOVIC
utterances.text: No, none.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Now, you said you didn't come across anyone, so I take it you didn't take anyone prisoner?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN JOVANOVIC
utterances.text: No. We took no prisoners and we found no dead bodies. We only found traces indicating that somebody left that area before we reached that place.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Had you been given specific instructions on what to do or how to treat any prisoners that you might have come across, in the eventuality that you came across?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN JOVANOVIC
utterances.text: We did not receive any specific instructions, but I told company commanders that in case we take any prisoners, they should be taken into custody.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: All right. Now, what did you do the following day, if you recall?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN JOVANOVIC
utterances.text: The next day, we started from Pale to continue our search of the terrain towards Jaglici.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: How long did that take?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN JOVANOVIC
utterances.text: I'm not sure. I think one day, maybe two.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did you come across any prisoners -- or did you take any prisoners, I should say, during that two-day period?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN JOVANOVIC
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did you come across any dead bodies during that two-day period?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN JOVANOVIC
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: After that, do you recall what you did?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN JOVANOVIC
utterances.text: After that, we deployed units across various locations, that is in certain villages, so that they could continue to search the terrain from those villages in the following days. That was our assignment.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And during those following days, did the 2nd Battalion ever capture anyone?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN JOVANOVIC
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Now, during that period, had you seen your commander, Colonel Blagojevic?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN JOVANOVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Could you please tell us, if you recall, the date and the place, please.

utterances.speaker: ZORAN JOVANOVIC
utterances.text: I cannot remember the date, but I saw him in the area of Jaglici.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Could you please tell us whether he was with anyone.

utterances.speaker: ZORAN JOVANOVIC
utterances.text: He was with Lieutenant Colonel Cvjetinovic.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Would you please tell us what was the nature of this meeting.

utterances.speaker: ZORAN JOVANOVIC
utterances.text: Well, he was there just to have a look around to see how we were doing, where we were, and if we were encountering any problems. That meeting did not last long.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did you tell him whether you had been encountering any problems?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN JOVANOVIC
utterances.text: We informed him that we had done what we were supposed to do, that we had not run into any problems, that we had no clashes with the enemy because we did not find any enemy, and that was it.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: All right. Now, after that meeting, did there some a time when you had another meeting with your commander, Colonel Blagojevic?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN JOVANOVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Could you please explain to us when that was, where, and what was the nature of the meeting.

utterances.speaker: ZORAN JOVANOVIC
utterances.text: I cannot remember the date again, but the meeting took place at the battalion command, the command of the 2nd Infantry Battalion. Colonel Blagojevic came to our command post and asked me to send one unit the size of a company to the Zvornik Brigade.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did Colonel Blagojevic explain to you the reasons why he wanted you to put a company together to send to the Zvornik Brigade?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN JOVANOVIC
utterances.text: No. He only said that he had received orders from his superiors, I suppose, that one company-sized unit should be sent as assistance to the Zvornik Brigade, but for what reason and on what mission, I didn't know.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Were you aware at that point in time what was happening in the Zvornik area?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN JOVANOVIC
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Now, did anything happen after that request was made?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN JOVANOVIC
utterances.text: You mean while I was putting together and sending that unit?

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Yes. Yes. I apologise for the inartful way of putting the question.

utterances.speaker: ZORAN JOVANOVIC
utterances.text: While designating that unit that was to be sent to the Zvornik Brigade, we found that the troops were very unhappy. I gathered one unit and lined it up outside our logistical base and informed them of where they were supposed to go. They started arguing, refusing the orders, and there ensued a heated argument between the troops and me and Commander Blagojevic.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: All right. And during that -- those activities, did anything else happen that you recall?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN JOVANOVIC
utterances.text: Well, ugly things were said on that occasion by the soldiers, addressed to Colonel Blagojevic and me. And some soldiers even pulled out their weapons.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And where did they point their weapons to?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN JOVANOVIC
utterances.text: Well, at Colonel Blagojevic.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Why was this discontent among the soldiers, and why would someone even point a weapon to their own commander?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN JOVANOVIC
utterances.text: Well, I suppose it was because the combat activities around Srebrenica were over, and they were supposed to continue on to Zvornik. They thought that Zvornik was a problematic area, and they were looking for reasons to refuse to go there. And those troops were from Bratunac originally.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: All right. Did the company eventually go to Zvornik?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN JOVANOVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Now, could you please tell us how you managed to -- you or Colonel Blagojevic managed to get the company to agree to go to Zvornik, in light of what you just told us.

utterances.speaker: ZORAN JOVANOVIC
utterances.text: I said to Colonel Blagojevic that he can go to his command post, that is to say the brigade command post, and that I will try, as the superior officer, to resolve this question and to somehow persuade them to go to carry out that assignment. I quarrelled with them for a long time there, too, and finally I said I would go down there with them. And it was after that that they got on to the bus.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: All right. Did you go all the way to Zvornik with them?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN JOVANOVIC
utterances.text: When we got into the bus, I said to the driver that he should drive the bus to the brigade command so that I could report to my superior officer, in view of the fact that I was going with them and that I was leaving the battalion behind. And if nothing else, to see what the number of soldiers who were leaving was, so that we would be aware of the number of personnel.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: All right. And did you do that?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN JOVANOVIC
utterances.text: Yes. I reported there. Lieutenant Colonel Cvjetinovic was there. I said to him that we were going down there, that I was going with them. And he said that that was out of the question, for me to go with a unit that is below the level of a company and that in this way I would be leaving the battalion without a commander. The task of the battalion for the following day was to go to Zepa, so they did not allow me to go with that group.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: All right. Did the group eventually go to Zvornik?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN JOVANOVIC
utterances.text: After having spoken to Lieutenant Colonel Cvjetinovic, I went back into the bus and I said to the soldiers who were on the bus that I was not allowed to go with them because the following day the remainder of the battalion was to be sent to the area of Zepa. It was then that they probably realised that it was all the same. If they were supposed to go to Zepa the following day, perhaps it was better for them to go to Zvornik now. So they did go and they caused no further trouble.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Who commanded that unit, if you recall?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN JOVANOVIC
utterances.text: That unit was commanded by Zoran Kovacevic. He was company commander otherwise, and most of the soldiers in that group were from his unit. He was already on the bus.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: All right. Do you know how long Zoran Kovacevic was in Zvornik?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN JOVANOVIC
utterances.text: I'm not sure, but I think they spent two nights there.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: When was the next time that you saw Mr. Kovacevic?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN JOVANOVIC
utterances.text: We saw each other at Zepa. The following day, I went with the remaining soldiers to Zepa. And after their returned from Zvornik, they came to Zepa, too.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did Mr. Kovacevic tell you what had occurred in -- when he went up to the Zvornik area?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN JOVANOVIC
utterances.text: Yes, yes. When he came up there, he informed me about where they were and what their task was.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: All right. So they ended up going to Zepa after all, to Zvornik and then Zepa?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN JOVANOVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Do you recall when you went to Zepa?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN JOVANOVIC
utterances.text: They went to Zvornik, and then the following day we went to Zepa.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Over the years have you heard whether any of the men that you sent to Zvornik under the command of Zoran Kovacevic, whether they were involved in any atrocities in that area?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN JOVANOVIC
utterances.text: No, no. Zoran Kovacevic informed me that they were used up there at Crni Vrh, along the road between Zvornik and Tuzla, and that they were not engaged in combat action at all.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Do you know to whom Mr. Kovacevic was to report once he arrived in Zvornik and the Zvornik Brigade, because I believe that's what you indicated earlier?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN JOVANOVIC
utterances.text: I don't know. I don't know. It was for us to appoint a unit, and somebody was probably supposed to take them there and hand them over to someone - I don't know who - at the Zvornik Brigade.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: All right. Now, I'm going to jump around from topic to topic, smaller topics. Do you recall either prior to or right around the fall of Srebrenica whether you were ever asked to provide someone to demine a section of a field or a path at or near the Zuti Most?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN JOVANOVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: All right. This is something that we're very curious to get to the bottom to. Could you please tell us: Who was it that came to you with this request?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN JOVANOVIC
utterances.text: A policeman came. I don't know. I can't remember his name. I didn't know him. But he came to the battalion headquarters and he asked me to give a soldier from the unit that was carrying out the mining in front of our defence line. At one part near Zuti Most, he was supposed to carry out demining so that passage would be made possible.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: All right. First of all, you said "policeman." Is this a military policeman or is this a MUP, civilian police?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN JOVANOVIC
utterances.text: Civilian police.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Now, was he from Bratunac or from someplace else, if you know?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN JOVANOVIC
utterances.text: He wasn't from the Bratunac MUP.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did you recognise this policeman?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN JOVANOVIC
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did the policeman indicate to you whether he had received orders for this particular request?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN JOVANOVIC
utterances.text: He said that they had sent him to convey to me that I was supposed to provide one of those persons that I mentioned just now for carrying out that particular assignment.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Do you know whether the "they," the person who had sent them, whether that person was in fact Colonel Blagojevic?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN JOVANOVIC
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did he ever mention that he had received authorisation from, or an order from Colonel Blagojevic in order to secure a deminer from you to demine part of the road?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: That's a lack of foundation and leading. The proper question is: Who did you receive the order from?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Yes. It's very leading.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Your Honour, he indicated that he didn't -- he didn't know. I don't mind, but I assume now, I assume, that Mr. McCloskey is going to be doing the cross-examination, because I see Mr. Shin there writing busily, being whispered into, and now we've got McCloskey jumping up. And I don't mind, I just want to know what the rules are because this is not procedural in nature. So I just thought I'd point that out, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Yes. But as for this particular question, I think it's a leading question.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Very well, Your Honour. I'll go about it another way. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did he say from whom he had received this order?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN JOVANOVIC
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Now, this may be leading, but I'm going to have to ask it and see whether I draw an objection. Did he mention Blagojevic at all?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN JOVANOVIC
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Okay. Did you contact your commander?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN JOVANOVIC
utterances.text: You mean that question, whether I could send that person in order to carry out the demining or --

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Right. Did you contact your commander, Colonel Blagojevic, to seek authorisation --

utterances.speaker: ZORAN JOVANOVIC
utterances.text: No, no. No, no.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did you contact anyone, Mladic, Krstic, or anyone?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN JOVANOVIC
utterances.text: No. No.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: All right. Did you provide that person, the deminer that is?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN JOVANOVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Do you know whether the demining took place?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN JOVANOVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Do you recall the exact date? That -- that's an important detail for them.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: I object to the little comments about what's important to the various parties. You know, this kind of comment and whether we're trying to trick somebody, I don't know what it's designed to do, but it's absolutely inappropriate.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Yes, I think that question is enough, you asking about the exact date.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Do you know the exact date?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN JOVANOVIC
utterances.text: I do not remember.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Do you know the time of day? Was it morning? Middle of the day? Middle of the afternoon? Or evening? Or any time in between?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN JOVANOVIC
utterances.text: I'm not sure. I think it was in the afternoon.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Do you recall for how long, how long, this deminer was preoccupied in demining the area that was requested?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN JOVANOVIC
utterances.text: I do not remember because he did not report after having completed the assignment.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: When the police officer came over to make this request, did you by any chance make any inquiries as to why they needed this area demined, the purpose?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN JOVANOVIC
utterances.text: He said that at that point they were supposed to enter Potocari.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did you ask him when they were supposed to enter Potocari?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN JOVANOVIC
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Now, when he said that "they were supposed to enter Potocari," who did you understand "they" to be?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN JOVANOVIC
utterances.text: I assumed it was the police.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Now, just as a point of reference if you could help us out here a little bit. You told us on the 12th, the day of Srebrenica fell, you received orders to move from your positions and search some terrain. Do you recall telling us that?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN JOVANOVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: This incident, or this activity I should say, because it's not really an incident, this activity, for you to provide a deminer, was that before that day or after?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN JOVANOVIC
utterances.text: Would you please repeat that question.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: When the police officer came to see you, whether you could give him a deminer, was that before or after you had left your positions to search the terrain towards Pale, Jaglici, and so on?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN JOVANOVIC
utterances.text: Before we left.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: All right. Now, during that period, incidentally, did you see Mr. Nikolic at all, Momir Nikolic?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN JOVANOVIC
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You knew him, did you not?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN JOVANOVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: In fact, if I understand you correctly -- as I understand your testimony, at one point you had been part of the intelligence and security?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN JOVANOVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Do you recall where during that period he had ever made any inquiries with respect to the security or intelligence situation in the field, on the ground?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN JOVANOVIC
utterances.text: Very little. For the most part during the war, I was assistant battalion commander for intelligence and security matters. In that period I do not remember that we ever had a meeting with Momir Nikolic in order to receive some instructions as to what we were supposed to do in the battalion with regard to security, intelligence, and so on. So it seems to me that he did not attach much importance to us in battalions who were engaged in this line of work.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Okay. Thank you. Now, I want to show you a map, and it's been marked for identification as D180. First of all, can you look at this map, sir, and ask -- and tell us whether you recognise it.

utterances.speaker: ZORAN JOVANOVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Now, are there some markings on this map?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN JOVANOVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Do you know who made those markings?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN JOVANOVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And could you please tell us who made the markings.

utterances.speaker: ZORAN JOVANOVIC
utterances.text: I did.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And when did you make those markings, sir?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN JOVANOVIC
utterances.text: In Banja Luka, when I went there to make a statement.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: So you made those markings on that map for the benefit of the Office of the Prosecution?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN JOVANOVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Now, before we got into the map itself, could you briefly tell us what was the purpose for marking the map.

utterances.speaker: ZORAN JOVANOVIC
utterances.text: They asked me to draw the line of defence of the 2nd Battalion until the fall of Srebrenica. And after that, to mark the movements of units with regard to searching the terrain, a subject we discussed a while ago.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: All right. Well, perhaps we can put it on the ELMO and you can then describe to us step by step what you marked so at least we can see. If you could -- sir, if you could show us the portion that would reflect -- if you could put it on the ELMO.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Thank you, Madam Usher.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: If you could show us where the lines of the 2nd Battalion is. And if you could look at the map itself when you point.

utterances.speaker: ZORAN JOVANOVIC
utterances.text: The position of the 2nd Battalion until the fall of Srebrenica, the yellow line marks Obadi on the left, the village of Obadi.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Okay. If we can just stick -- let's stay here for a second. Now, the yellow line reflects what? Are those the defence lines?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN JOVANOVIC
utterances.text: Yes, yes. It's the defence line that we held until the fall of Srebrenica.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Okay. Now, on which side -- now, we see a road there, do we not?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN JOVANOVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Okay. If you could please just point to us, where is the Zuti Most located.

utterances.speaker: ZORAN JOVANOVIC
utterances.text: [Witness complies]

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: All right. And could you please tell us where is the 3rd and 4th Companies located.

utterances.speaker: ZORAN JOVANOVIC
utterances.text: The 3rd and 4th Company are on the left, left of the road from Bratunac to Srebrenica, Caus, and Obad.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: All right. If we could move the map just slightly up so we can see where Potocari is.

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: The interpreter could not hear the witness.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Okay. Could you show us where Potocari is, the village Potocari. Let's start with that first.

utterances.speaker: ZORAN JOVANOVIC
utterances.text: This is where the village of Potocari is.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Okay. Now, what is the area commonly referred to Potocari? Not the village but the area.

utterances.speaker: ZORAN JOVANOVIC
utterances.text: Along the road here, along the Bratunac/Srebrenica road.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Okay. And could you please tell us -- I understand there are some industrial buildings there. Could you please point to us where those buildings would be located on the map.

utterances.speaker: ZORAN JOVANOVIC
utterances.text: On the left- and right-hand side of the road towards Srebrenica. On the right side and on the left side here.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Okay. And you were pointing where it says Pecista. Is that it? Is that where the buildings would be located, right around that area?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN JOVANOVIC
utterances.text: They are below the village of Pecista, closer to the road.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Now, in looking at the yellow line that we have where the 3rd and 4th Companies are, could you please tell us what the terrain looks like, what the terrain is like actually.

utterances.speaker: ZORAN JOVANOVIC
utterances.text: There is a forest there. It's hilly terrain, a forested -- very inaccessible. And the slopes are steep.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Okay. Now, when the -- when you get out of the forest and you reach the bottom of the hill, how close is it to the road itself? What's the distance?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN JOVANOVIC
utterances.text: From the outskirts of the forest to the road, there is about 1.000 metres, perhaps a bit less.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And how close would it be to where the industrial buildings are located?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN JOVANOVIC
utterances.text: The industrial buildings are much closer to the edge of the forest, much closer than the road is. They are about 3 or 400 metres away.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: From where you were located, were you able to see, on the 12th that is, where the population -- the mass of people had gathered in Potocari, in and around Potocari?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN JOVANOVIC
utterances.text: Yes. I was here in the area of the village of Zagoni at this checkpoint. I can't see the number here. From the place where I was, I could see Potocari and everything else down there.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Now, could you see them on the 11th, the day before, as they were gathering or coming --

utterances.speaker: ZORAN JOVANOVIC
utterances.text: Yes, yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Were you ever given any instructions to attack the population?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN JOVANOVIC
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did you, on your own, attack the population?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN JOVANOVIC
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: All right. Now, looking at the map, again if we could get back to the Zuti Most, which is I believe you indicated near -- where on the map it says 212, but actually it's right on the road, but just as a point of reference. Could you please show us where the 2nd, 1st and -- or 2nd, 5th, 1st Companies would have been located.

utterances.speaker: ZORAN JOVANOVIC
utterances.text: To the right of the road, this yellow line that was marked here, it was the 2nd Company first, then parts of the 1st Company, and then the 5th Company.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Now, if we could move the map down just slightly. Okay. Thank you. Now, could you please show us on the map which route you took on that first day, the 12th that is, when you moved from your position to search the terrain, as you had been ordered to?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN JOVANOVIC
utterances.text: We went through the village of Zagoni to the road, from Budak to --

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: The interpreter could not hear the last word. Could the witness please speak into the microphone.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Okay. I need you to speak a little louder or speak into the microphone, and if you could show us just slowly, again with the pointer.

utterances.speaker: ZORAN JOVANOVIC
utterances.text: All right. So through the village of Zagoni, the village road leads to the road that goes from Potocari and Budak to Bljeceva. That's where we went down to this road.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And do you know how other members of the 2nd Company, how they arrived in that area, because we talked about that they had to go through Budak? Could you please show us on the map.

utterances.speaker: ZORAN JOVANOVIC
utterances.text: One part came along this line that we had held until then up there, and another part came from this demined area. That was what we discussed a while ago in connection with the police. So they got down here to the road before Zagoni, and then we met up here. We got together there.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Would you please show us from the asphalt road where is the turn-off to go to Budak.

utterances.speaker: ZORAN JOVANOVIC
utterances.text: They did not take an asphalt road to this road that leads to Bljeceva. From the defence line that we held over here, they went through the demined minefield. And along the outskirts of the forest over here, they got up here to this road.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Were you with that group?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN JOVANOVIC
utterances.text: No, I was at Zagoni, over here at Kaolin, and I went down here with these parts of the unit.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Would it surprise --

utterances.speaker: ZORAN JOVANOVIC
utterances.text: But that's not very far away. It can actually be seen with a naked eye. I could actually see those parts of the units that were up there.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Do you know whether any of your men went into Potocari?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN JOVANOVIC
utterances.text: I found out that there were some.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did you authorise that?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN JOVANOVIC
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Your Honour, this might be a good time for the break.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Yes, we'll have a break and we'll resume at 12.30.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Karnavas.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Now, sir, would you please look at the map again and show us what these other markings indicate, starting with the red markings. What are those markings?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN JOVANOVIC
utterances.text: The red lines indicate the positions of the units that were supposed to take up position after moving from their initial lines. The 4th and the 3rd companies were supposed to take up positions at Djogazi and Pecista. The 2nd Company, the part of the 1st and the 5th Mekote and --

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Another place name was missed by the interpreter.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: What was the other place that you indicated?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN JOVANOVIC
utterances.text: Budak and Mekote village, which is near Bljeceva.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Could you please explain to us what the blue markings relate to.

utterances.speaker: ZORAN JOVANOVIC
utterances.text: This marking probably indicates nothing in particular. It just indicates which company takes up position on which line, in which area.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: All right. Now, I want to show you a series of documents, if we could go through them rather quickly. The first one will be what has been entered into evidence as P469. This is a daily combat report dated 13 July 1995. If you could look at this document, and you're being provided with a handwritten version, with the ERN number 00675013. If you could look at it and tell us whether there's anything in this particular daily combat report that would reflect activities carried out by your battalion. Look at paragraph number 2.

utterances.speaker: ZORAN JOVANOVIC
utterances.text: Reference is made here to Ravni Buljim, which is a hill that was in front of us. And it was up to that place that we were supposed to search the terrain, right behind Likari village I believe the name was, right below Jaglici.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And was that reflected in the map that you showed us, the lines that you had drawn for the Office of the Prosecution back in 2001? I beg your pardon? You need to speak up so they can hear you.

utterances.speaker: ZORAN JOVANOVIC
utterances.text: Right. Okay.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Now, if I can show you the next document, P483. This is an order dated 14 July 1995. Please look at it. Please tell us whether you have ever seen this particular document.

utterances.speaker: ZORAN JOVANOVIC
utterances.text: Yes, I have seen this document.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Now, if you look at paragraph number 2 in the order, it talks about the 2nd Battalion, does it not?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN JOVANOVIC
utterances.text: Yes, it does.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And does that accurately -- now, in comparison to the map that we've seen earlier, are these the tasks that you carried out in searching the terrain?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN JOVANOVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And this was pointed out to you on the map -- this is what you pointed out to the Prosecution when you drew the coordinates on the map?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN JOVANOVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you. Okay. Is there anything else that might be of some significance to your particular battalion in this particular order?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN JOVANOVIC
utterances.text: Nothing in particular.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: All right. Now, I want to show you one other document. This is a daily combat report dated 15 July 1995. If you could please look at it and please tell us first of all whether there's any particular section in this daily combat report that would be of some relevance to the 2nd Battalion. You may wish to focus your attention on paragraph number 2.

utterances.speaker: ZORAN JOVANOVIC
utterances.text: I don't see anything in particular, apart from the fact that a part of the troops from our battalion were sent to the 2nd Romanija Motorised Brigade.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Okay. Why were they sent there, do you know?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN JOVANOVIC
utterances.text: Even before, in the preceding period, we used to send a certain number of soldiers to hold the line.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Okay. Thank you. Now, if we could go back to what has been marked as D179 for identification. That was your -- a copy of your notebook, the one that the Office of the Prosecution located at the Bratunac Brigade headquarters. I just want to walk you through several of these days, starting with the 6th of July. You will see that there is a date 6 and 7th --

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Microphone, please.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You will see that there is a -- and you will find it on the top of the page. There is a number 01134049. Do you see that?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN JOVANOVIC
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Okay. And there you -- we see that it says: "Deployment of officers." These officers, who are they?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN JOVANOVIC
utterances.text: Those are officers of the command of the 2nd Battalion.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: All right.

utterances.speaker: ZORAN JOVANOVIC
utterances.text: And this is a deployment of officers that I made to designate who will go to which unit.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Now, there's also a note here with respect to "Miladin Vuksic for Monday - the Court." Do you know Miladin Vuksic?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN JOVANOVIC
utterances.text: Yes, Miladin Vuksic was a soldier in the 2nd Company, I think, of the 2nd Infantry Battalion.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Do you know what this is in reference to, "the Court"?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN JOVANOVIC
utterances.text: I don't know. It must have been some private business of his.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Now, if we go down to the next page, this would be page 4 in the English version, on the next page of your page it says: "Number of shells fired on 6 and 7." These are your notes, are they not, sir?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN JOVANOVIC
utterances.text: Yes, they are.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: What do these -- what do these notes reflect?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN JOVANOVIC
utterances.text: Well, that indicates the number of shells fired by us during those days, on the 6th and the 7th.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: All right. Now, the next notation that we have here that I want you to look at, at least, is 8 July 1995. Do you see that?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN JOVANOVIC
utterances.text: Yes, I do.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And what does that reflect, sir?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN JOVANOVIC
utterances.text: Also the number of shells fired for that day.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Now, after that we go to July 15. And so we don't have any notes for the 9th, 10th, 11th, 12th, 13th, 14th, nor do we have any indication, at least from the Office of the Prosecution, that those pages were torn off or destroyed. So could you please explain to us: Why are there no notes for those days?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN JOVANOVIC
utterances.text: Well, nothing special or out of the ordinary happened in those days, and that's why no notes were made.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: All right. Now, right under 15 July 1995, you have 7.00 a.m., and then you jump right to 20 July 1995. And it says: "Replacement in Trnovo, reduction of battalion to resistance points," and so on. What does that refer to, this replacement in Trnovo? What does that mean?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN JOVANOVIC
utterances.text: We also sent a certain number of soldiers to Trnovo because we were holding a line there as well. And that means that on the 20th July at 7.00 we were to prepare that number of soldiers who were to take over at Trnovo, to replace the people who had been there for a while.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And then if we went further down, it says: "Deployment of 2nd Infantry Battalion." And it says: "Zagoni, Pale," and so on. Do you know what's that's in reference to? Is that for the date of July 15 --

utterances.speaker: ZORAN JOVANOVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Is that for the date of July 15th or is that for the date of July 20th?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN JOVANOVIC
utterances.text: No, no. That's from the 15th onwards. Deployment of units across these villages for the purposes of searching the terrain in the period that followed.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And then we also see on that same column, the last item, you indicate -- and that would be on the next page, page 6 in the English version, it states there: "54 conscript from the 4th Infantry," and something about Crni Vrh. Do you see that?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN JOVANOVIC
utterances.text: Yes, I can see that.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And could you please tell us what that's about.

utterances.speaker: ZORAN JOVANOVIC
utterances.text: That's the unit that was to go and assist the Zvornik Brigade. We talked about it earlier.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: All right. And then we can also -- the next item is July 16th, and in fact there you even have a notation that there was a meeting of company commanders. Do you see that, where it says: "List of replacements" --

utterances.speaker: ZORAN JOVANOVIC
utterances.text: Yes, yes, I see that.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Okay. Now, do you know what this was in relation to, this meeting? Who was there? Where was it held?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN JOVANOVIC
utterances.text: Meeting with company commanders regarding upcoming tasks. Appointment of troops for replacement at Trnovo, and the plane of engagement of conscripts for deployment in villages, in areas that we discussed earlier. And also a list of conscripts who were to be designated to replace units at Pjenovac.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And Pjenovac, what was going on there that you needed to replace the tasks?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN JOVANOVIC
utterances.text: At Pjenovac, this document that you showed me a moment ago referred to the second Romanija Brigade. There as well we had a number of troops and we needed to replace the men who had been there for some time.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And this was something that had been going on prior to any activities concerning Srebrenica?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN JOVANOVIC
utterances.text: Yes, yes. That was the regular replacement we carried out before.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Okay. Thank you. I don't have any more questions regarding this particular document. Incidentally, I just want to go back to that issue when we talked about, the demining request that had been made of you to provide someone to demine that area when the police officer came. Was -- were any incidents with respect to that particular task, were there any incidents?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN JOVANOVIC
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Do you know whether during this demining process or any other demining process from deminers from the 2nd Battalion, whether any of them lost their lives while demining?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN JOVANOVIC
utterances.text: I remember that one of them got killed by a mine.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Do you know where that would have been, what was the -- where it was, the circumstances?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN JOVANOVIC
utterances.text: I don't know, but I believe it was somewhere in that area, precisely where these mines were being deactivated.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Okay. Thank you, sir, I have no further questions. Mr. Stojanovic may have some questions, he represents Mr. Jokic. The Prosecutor, one of them - they're both jumping up - but one of them might have some questions for you, and perhaps the Judges. I would appreciate if you could be as frank and honest with them as you have been with me. Thank you very much, sir.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: I have no further questions, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. Karnavas. Mr. Stojanovic, do you have any questions for this witness?

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Good morning, Your Honour. Good morning, Witness. Your Honour, we have no questions for this witness, bearing in mind his testimony today.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. Stojanovic. Any cross-examination? Yes, Mr. McCloskey?

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. President, Your Honours. Cross-examined by Mr. McCloskey:

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Good afternoon, sir.

utterances.speaker: ZORAN JOVANOVIC
utterances.text: Good afternoon.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Going back to your notes where you say you provided 54 people, those were the 54 people that went to Zvornik?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN JOVANOVIC
utterances.text: 54 were supposed to be sent, but I don't believe that many of them actually left. However, that was a unit that was sent to Zvornik.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: How many from your battalion do you think actually went?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN JOVANOVIC
utterances.text: Less than 50.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: About how many, if you know?

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: I'm sorry, I'm getting a buzz in my ear again.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Between 35 and 50. I can't tell you more precisely.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Okay. And so if we go back to that daily combat report on the 15th, it talks about 80 people going up to Zvornik. Do you know where the other, I don't know, roughly 30 or 40 people came from that would have gone up to Zvornik?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN JOVANOVIC
utterances.text: One bus left for Zvornik and it wasn't full. There was certainly less than 50 men.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: So you think this daily combat report is not correct when it says 80 men went up to Zvornik that day?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN JOVANOVIC
utterances.text: No, it certainly isn't correct. I know that one bus left for Zvornik because I was supposed to go with them. And I know for certain there were less than 50 men. No more than 50 can be seated on a bus. There was certainly less than 50.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Okay. Well, that's the bus from your battalion, but couldn't the Bratunac command have sent up another bus or another truck on the same day or near the same time to meet this roughly 80 number on their report?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN JOVANOVIC
utterances.text: No. I was there when they left from the command, because I was supposed originally to go with them. However, they left me behind and I was present when they departed for Zvornik. There were only soldiers from my battalion; there were no other reinforcements, no other assistance from other troops.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: How long were you at the command after the bus left?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN JOVANOVIC
utterances.text: I returned very soon to the command post of my battalion.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: So you don't know after you left the command whether or not Blagojevic sent up another vehicle with Zvornik -- up to Zvornik?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN JOVANOVIC
utterances.text: I don't know.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: So do you have any reason to believe this 80 figure was deliberately false?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN JOVANOVIC
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Okay. Now, when you pick your 54 guys, or 50, or a little less, how did you decide who had to go to Zvornik?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN JOVANOVIC
utterances.text: Colonel Blagojevic ordered me to send one company. I decided to appoint the 4th Company, commanded by Zoran Kovacevic, because at that moment they were free. They were not otherwise engaged. And the company numbered more than 50 men. However, we were hard-put to put together even those who actually left.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Why didn't you send any 3rd Company?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN JOVANOVIC
utterances.text: The 3rd Company was involved in an assignment.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Is that the same -- true of the 2nd and the 1st that didn't get sent, because they were involved in assignments as well?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN JOVANOVIC
utterances.text: Yes. In that period, a lot of troops were already out in the field, in the area between Pjenovac and Trnovo. And we didn't have enough troops left because some were on leave and others were engaged in the missions we had at the time.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: So you know -- you knew at the time what your other companies were doing when you decided to send the 4th Company up to Zvornik?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN JOVANOVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: In fact, as a commander, you had to evaluate what each of your companies were doing in order to choose the one you wanted to go meet that order to go to Zvornik. Right?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN JOVANOVIC
utterances.text: No. I knew where these other companies were deployed, and the 4th Company at that moment was free. That's why I appointed them to go.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Maybe you misunderstood me, but you had to know what each of your companies was doing in order to choose the company that you actually ended up choosing?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN JOVANOVIC
utterances.text: I knew everything. I knew what each company was doing.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: As a commander, that was your responsibility, wasn't it?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN JOVANOVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did Colonel Blagojevic talk to you about potentially sending people to Zepa along with Zvornik when he talked to you about Zvornik?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN JOVANOVIC
utterances.text: At that moment, there was no question of sending troops to Zepa.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Okay. But you've seen this daily combat report on the 13th where it talks about -- the brigade is working on getting a group together to be sent to Zepa. Right?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN JOVANOVIC
utterances.text: The 1st Battalion had gone to Zepa before, in which period exactly I don't know. All I know is that the 1st Battalion had been to Zepa before. So maybe that referred to them.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: All I'm asking you is that it's clear from this 13 July report that Colonel Blagojevic has to follow orders and get a unit and send them off to Zepa on the 13th. Right?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN JOVANOVIC
utterances.text: I only know of the orders that I got from Colonel Blagojevic that had to do with the 2nd Battalion.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: I know. I'm just asking you about this daily combat report; it's as simple as that. It got read to you by the Defence. It says: "The brigade command is working on the formation of a company to be sent to the area of Podravanje to carry out the assignment." That's 469. So is it fair to say that if that's true, Colonel Blagojevic on the 13th had to work to find a unit to send towards this assignment? I'm not trying to --

utterances.speaker: ZORAN JOVANOVIC
utterances.text: Which area?

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: -- I'm just trying to ask you about this order. It's a very simple question. It says he's working on sending somebody to Zepa -- or to Podravanje.

utterances.speaker: ZORAN JOVANOVIC
utterances.text: I beg your pardon.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: It says he's working on sending someone to Podravanje, do you have any doubt in your mind that that's what he's working on that day, based on this order?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN JOVANOVIC
utterances.text: We sent a unit from the battalion, a platoon actually with Major Pajic to the area of Milici or Podravanje. I don't remember the exact date, but we did send this one unit.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: The records and the other records show that Major Pajic led that unit, which is the subject of the order I just read to you. So knowing that, is it fair to say Colonel Blagojevic had to send that unit. Right?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN JOVANOVIC
utterances.text: The unit left with Major Pajic to the area of Podravanje. That's the way it was.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And would Colonel Blagojevic have been involved in that process of getting that unit together and making sure they got off to the assignment?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN JOVANOVIC
utterances.text: Major Pajic came to me and said that I should get a unit that would go to the area of Podravanje, and that he would lead and command that unit.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Okay. Listen to my question. Would Colonel Blagojevic have been involved in that process to get Pajic and his unit ready and off to that assignment?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN JOVANOVIC
utterances.text: Colonel Blagojevic did not issue an order to me. Maybe he did to Major Pajic, but Pajic came to me with an order that I should get a unit together and that he would lead that unit.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Okay. Let me just go back to my sort of general question that we talked about. We'll go back to you as a commander. In order to meet the orders that were provided to you by your superiors to get a unit ready to go to Zvornik, you, as you said, had to decide which of your companies to send, and you did, because they were the company that was free. Now, if, just if, if Colonel Blagojevic got a similar order to get one of his units and send them somewhere, would he have had to have gone through the same basic process that you did, see which of his units were available, figure out who could be sent? It's a very simple question.

utterances.speaker: ZORAN JOVANOVIC
utterances.text: No, no.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Now, he wouldn't have had to do that. What would he have done?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN JOVANOVIC
utterances.text: He ordered me to get a company that would go to Zvornik, and it was my decision that it would be the 4th Company. He did not tell me at any point in time that I should send the 4th Company or the 2nd Company or any other specific unit.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Okay. But I'm asking you a little bit different. I'm asking you about a hypothetical of what your commander would have been involved in. Before your commander would have asked you, wouldn't he have had to know what the other battalions were doing in order to determine which lucky person would have to send people to Zvornik?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN JOVANOVIC
utterances.text: I don't know for what reason he decided to ask me for a company. It wasn't for me to ask why he asked me from the 2nd Battalion for a company.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: But as a commander, as a commander, wouldn't Blagojevic have had to know what his other battalions were doing before he asked you? I'm not asking you to tell me why. I'm just asking you: As a commander, wouldn't he have had to know what his other battalions were doing?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN JOVANOVIC
utterances.text: He probably did know what the other battalions were doing, but I, as his subordinate, was not supposed to ask him about things like that. My duty was to carry out the order that I got, namely to select a company that would be sent to Zvornik.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Okay. And if one of your companies happened to be guarding prisoners at the time you got an order like this, would you have known that they were guarding prisoners?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN JOVANOVIC
utterances.text: I'm sorry. Could you repeat that question.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: If when you got this order from Blagojevic to get a unit together to go to Zvornik and one of your companies had - and I'm not saying it did, because I know you said it didn't - but had they been guarding prisoners at the time in your area, would you have known it?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN JOVANOVIC
utterances.text: Of course I would have known it.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Now, when Colonel Blagojevic is, as the commander of the brigade, considering what units he might send to Zepa or send to Zvornik, can you tell me what different units he would have had to choose from. We know yours. What else? And I'm not saying which ones, but normally which units would he look at as potential people to send somewhere?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN JOVANOVIC
utterances.text: Well, we did not have any special units in the battalion. We had companies with the kind of age pattern that prevailed. I think that the 1st Battalion was already at Zepa at the time, so there was no other option but to select a unit from the 2nd Battalion. Perhaps that was the reason why the colonel asked us to send a company.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: He would ideally want someone that was perhaps better disciplined than your standard conscript in a trench?

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Your Honour, all of them were --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: -- conscripts and all of them were in trenches, so if he can distinguish.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: That's not true.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: I don't know whether this gentleman had any specialised troops, so if he could lay a foundation, but I'm unaware of the 2nd Battalion having any you know commando-type, disciplined troops.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: The witness, Your Honour, is not speaking now of the 2nd Battalion, he just spoke of the 1st Battalion, and he said the reason they came to the 2nd Battalion was because other people were sent other places. My question is very simple: Wouldn't they want someone who was a little more disciplined than this usual trench soldier, and I can go through the units of the Bratunac Brigade for us, but I don't -- I would rather leave it up to the witness.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Well, generally speaking, you can proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Sir, what other -- is it true that Colonel Blagojevic would want to send someone a bit more disciplined, like you've suggested, and perhaps a younger age to be able to handle such an assignment?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN JOVANOVIC
utterances.text: All our companies were the same on average, as regards the number of personnel and the age pattern. Not a single one of these companies figured prominently in any respect compared to others. So had I sent any one of these companies to Zvornik, they would not have been anything special in relation to others.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: I'm not talking about your companies; I'm talking about brigade-wide. What other units would the -- Colonel Blagojevic have chosen from brigade-wide that were part of the Bratunac Brigade?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN JOVANOVIC
utterances.text: Well, within the Bratunac Brigade, we had four battalions. In all these battalions, there were companies, troops, that held the line during the war. We had the military police that carried out its own tasks. We did not have any other special units, no units of a special kind, if I can put it that way. So had he asked for a unit from another battalion, again it would have had to have been a company.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Were you aware of Rade Petrovic's Red Berets?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN JOVANOVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: It's a little different unit than the usual guys in most of the companies, isn't it?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN JOVANOVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: So do you want to consider your answer again? There are some special units in the Bratunac Brigade that he could have picked, aren't there? Rade Petrovic, for example.

utterances.speaker: ZORAN JOVANOVIC
utterances.text: Rade Petrovic's unit was a squad, that is 10 to 15 soldiers all together. Colonel Blagojevic wanted a unit at company level, so that required a larger number of soldiers. Why that particular unit was not used at all, I really don't know.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: I have the roster of that unit, and it shows, for July, 20 people. Now, Colonel Blagojevic could have sent the MP platoon as a combat unit, couldn't he?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN JOVANOVIC
utterances.text: He could have, but it was not for me to ask why he did not send the military police or I don't know what other unit. He strictly issued me an order to select a company that was supposed to go to Zvornik, and that was my task. It was not for me to ask him why he was not sending this group or that group.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: I don't have any further questions.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Thank you. Any re-direct?

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Again, Your Honour, this cross calls for no re-direct.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: Mr. President --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: I haven't said anything, but these comments about "this cross calls for no direct," these are argumentative, designed for a jury frankly. And they're never allowed where Mr. Karnavas comes from that I'm aware, and it becomes, you know, it does not become this international institution to listen to this each time.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Your Honour, I meant no offence. You know, when a cross deserves or is necessary for me to follow-up on re-direct, I do so. And I have been told to restrict it, to curtail it. So I've elongated my direct, and so I'm merely -- but if the gentleman is upset by what I'm saying, I'll delete that from my phraseology.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: There must be something to indicate your intention.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: That's why I said that there was no -- because the cross itself, there was no need for me to do re-direct --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: I know, I know. But maybe the wording. You might think of some better wording.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Okay. All right.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: I myself don't know how to put it.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: I'll work on it, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: I do have a couple of documents that we made reference to, and that would be D180. That was the map that the gentleman had marked when he was questioned by the Prosecution some two years after Mr. Blagojevic was indicted. And then D179, which are the notes from the work -- his own notebook which he referred to, just the limited pages -- well, actually the whole notebook can come in or the pages that he just made reference to, but we have the entire document.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Thank you. Any objections?

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: No, Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Thank you. I think I have a question concerning document D179/1. What's the relevance for this document?

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Well, Your Honour, I'm not dying to get it in. We don't have to have it introduced into evidence. Merely because he made reference to it, I thought as a courtesy if the Trial Chamber wished to have it. But in light of the fact that there's no dilemma, in the sense that there is no conflict as to what he said and what the other documents that already have been admitted, such as the daily combat reports, and -- so I'll withdraw that document. But the map, I do believe, is somewhat helpful, especially since he marked it and it does dovetail his testimony.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. McCloskey.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: I would then offer that document into evidence. I think the fact that there's nothing on it from 9 July until 15 July in combination with his testimony regarding that date is something the Court should consider and as well as the numbers of men being sent to various units might be helpful to have that as part of the record.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: But I myself have a question to this witness, if I could ask this witness concerning with the documents.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Absolutely, Your Honour, absolutely. Questioned by the Court:

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Well, Witness, in this document you listed several firings from your company. For instance, the number of shells fired on July 6th and 7th, 1995. Can I know which direction those shells were fired. Is it to Srebrenica?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN JOVANOVIC
utterances.text: Not at Srebrenica. With these weapons that were used for firing, we did not have the right range to reach Srebrenica. They were fired at the defence line that was right in front of ours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Thank you. I guess there's no questions out of my question?

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: No, Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Thank you. Well, I think these two documents are admitted into the evidence. If the Defence withdraws the document D179, the Prosecution will have it tendered. So we might have a Prosecution number, but I hope the parties will consult with the Court Deputy to solve this issue. To me, the number is not a big issue. Well, Witness, thank you very much for coming to The Hague to give your evidence. The usher will show you out of the room, and we wish you a pleasant journey back home. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Well, we still have 25 minutes left. Are there any witnesses waiting outside, Mr. Karnavas?

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Regrettably, no, Your Honour. He is here in The Hague. I didn't think that we would be so efficient. But, as I've indicated, I do anticipate sticking to the schedule that we had anticipated last week, that is that we would get all our witness plus make up for last week.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Thank you. There are some procedural matters. The first thing is that, Mr. Karnavas, we are expecting your reply today or tomorrow. I want to know what's the status for it, because we cannot do anything without receiving your reply.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Right. I had heard earlier that the Court would welcome it tomorrow, so in light of that bit of news I believe I will be able to have it tomorrow. We have it in the drafting stage, I just need to fine-tune it a little bit. We can even argue it a bit tomorrow, if need be, if there's time. But it will be in tomorrow. Now, I cannot guarantee that it will be in tomorrow morning at 9.00, but I will have it in tomorrow. That's a fixed date, and I think that's fair enough.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Well, I think during the last time we didn't say that there must be a hearing. It depends on the reply from the Defence counsel. So I just said that there might be. We could only make any decisions after reading those submissions.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Well, if the Court is leaning towards an adverse decision towards the Defence, I would welcome the opportunity to have an oral argument. If the Trial Chamber then is more inclined to deny the Prosecution's motion, then obviously I would have no need to present my views.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Well, the second issue is about the additional evidence concerning Witness P130.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Well --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: I am not sure what's the result of your consultations between the parties. Are there any developments? Because we would like to be informed as early as possible, so as to arrange some time, if necessary.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honour. Thank you. I notice that Mr. McCloskey is on his feet, but since I was already on my feet, rather than sit down and jump up again, let me just reply. We've heard that there was a meeting between Mr. McCloskey and Mr. Stojanovic and Mr. Lukic. And they've expressed their position that, at least as far as they're concerned - and I don't want to speak for them but I will at this stage - that they have no burning desire to re-open the case, simply for this gentleman to appear and testify, in light of the fact that his credibility is called into question. We received -- yesterday, we received a -- one of these CDs where you can hear the conversations, and I've spent a considerable time, both thinking about this and also looking at the issue itself. At this stage, I would first of all -- I would need to look at the CD -- hear it in a more thorough fashion. However, however, the Trial Chamber has been rather -- I will just say inflexible, for lack of a better term, in trying for us to meet our targeted date. I'm not saying that the Trial Chamber is being unreasonable, I'm just saying rather inflexible. We wish to comply with that, and we feel that in order to comply with that, we would have to proceed as we are proceeding. If there were to be a situation where the Prosecution were to re-open its case, it would require, I believe in order to -- for us to ethically meet our obligations to have some time to investigate, because it's not just a matter of the cross-examination of the gentleman, but also to see whether we would be able to find witnesses in addition to what we already have on the list. So we're talking about, one, adding more witnesses as a result of this; and two, some period. And so we're talking about some delay in the process, a delay which I believe I can speak for the Trial Chamber is one that they don't look at favourably. Be that as it may, that argument, let's set that aside. I've also thought about the situation where we are today. The Trial Chamber has already made a ruling, issued a judgement of acquittal, on several portions of the indictment. By re-opening the Prosecution's case at this stage, theoretically speaking, I don't think we have any jurisprudence at this stage in this Tribunal, but theoretically speaking the Prosecution could also argue that by re-opening its case, especially with the consent of the Defence, they would be entitled to the Trial Chamber also reconsidering the judgement of acquittal. And of course once a battle has been won, why would one need to fight it and win it all over again. So there is that concern. Also, I've given this some -- a great deal of thought. And it would seem to me that in no way is the trial -- is the Prosecution prejudiced by bringing this individual in as part of their rebuttal, in the event the Defence chooses not to call him. Now, as I said, I haven't listened to the entire transcript, but from what I understand it would appear, at a minimum, the gentleman committed perjury when he testified. So now it's a matter of cross-examining an acknowledged perjurer. And it would seem to me, as perhaps this became evident to the Jokic Defence, why would one need to examine a perjurer, who's already perjured himself in this particular case. We also believe that some of the testimony -- some of the facts he's given the Prosecution are rather incredible. And if the Prosecution wishes to put him on, then they can put him on in their case -- in their rebuttal, and then, of course, I would suspect that the Trial Chamber would allow us for surrebuttal, if there is any required. So, again, I haven't looked at it to see whether I would be calling the gentleman, but my instincts as a trial lawyer tell me that there is no need to build a wall only to knock it down, and so why would I want to call someone to cross-examine who now tells us is a perjurer who is also choosing other Prosecution witnesses - star witnesses, might I add - as perjurers, why would I need to do that? And so in all likelihood I will not be calling him as my witness, especially if we are going to meet the deadline that you have imposed on us. Because I can see that perhaps in the future we may be running over schedule with some of the witnesses. I don't know if I have been able to answer the Trial Chamber's question, but I think that's my position as of now. And I doubt if I'm going to reconsider -- at least the portion with allowing the Prosecution to re-open its case, only in the sense that at least they had an opportunity to put on their witness, he took an oath, the oath there says quite clearly: "The truth, the whole truth, and nothing but the truth," not part of the truth, not some of the truth, not some of the time, but all of the time, and, so, that's our position at this point. I did in fact let the -- I just want to clear, my initial instincts yesterday were to allow the Prosecution to go ahead as a courtesy. However, thinking about it again, in light of the judgement of acquittal, you know, had it gone any other way, which it could not, I dare say, but had it gone any other way, in other words, had it been disfavourable to us, I might have said: No harm, no foul. But in this instance I don't want to put myself in a position where I'm going to have to re-litigate points or issues or charges that have already been judged to have been found lacking in evidence. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Thank you very much for letting us know about your position at this moment. There is only one thing I would like to point out, that is you misused a word "perjurer." It should be alleged.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Well, Your Honour, he's admitted that --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: I understand that.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Okay. I will use -- well, defence lawyers usually get criticised for using the word "alleged."

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: I know that. Yes, Mr. McCloskey.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: Well, that is of course a curve ball thrown at us. That is a change, which everyone has a right to change their mind. But I spoke to Mr. Stojanovic. He was going to consult and I would be curious on his viewpoint, and then I could offer mine.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Thank you. Mr. Stojanovic.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, Your Honour. We did have a meeting yesterday with the Prosecutor, and our main subject was the issue of re-opening or not re-opening the Prosecution case at this stage, starting with new testimony by P130. We agreed - and the Prosecutor will correct me if I'm wrong - that at this point neither the Prosecution nor our Defence team are able to say whether we would be considering, contemplating, this at all. In our view, the Prosecution should use substantial evidence to test the credibility of P130. And it is also our view that, considering the drastic change of P130's testimony, it would be appropriate at least to let us have an insight into the statement made by this witness on the 23rd of May, on Sunday. I pointed out to Mr. McCloskey at least three Prosecution witnesses who have been heard by this Honourable Trial Chamber and said things completely opposite to the assertions of this new testimony by P130. These were not protected witnesses I believe, but certainly if we get to see this witness's statement and familiarise ourselves with it, we would be able to decide more competently. Also, when I was talking yesterday to Mr. McCloskey, I undertook to review all the substantial evidence we have and compare it with the statement of P130. And I believe that there is evidence on record that runs counter to the statements P130. However, we need some breathing space, some additional time to see whether it would be worthwhile to have this witness appear again or not. I said yesterday to Mr. McCloskey something that I think I should repeat here today; namely, that I as Defence counsel see nothing that I would gain my hearing him again.
